title: Clathrin: The Protein That Builds a Cage
description:
How does a cell bring substances in from the outside?
Clathrin is a protein that assembles into a cage-like structure beneath the cell membrane. As clathrin molecules gather, they help bend the membrane and form a small vesicle that carries selected molecules into the cell.
Once the vesicle is released, the clathrin coat quickly disassembles and the proteins are recycled for the next round.
Step inside the cell and watch this remarkable molecular machinery at work in 360° VR.

description:
The Fujian Tulou is one of China’s most fascinating architectural forms. These massive rammed-earth structures were built by the Hakka people, originally designed as fortresses to defend against enemy attacks. Their interiors are so spacious that an entire village could live within a single building. As time passed, these structures were no longer threatened by war, but the family-centered values and communal lifestyle they represent have endured.

title: I Have Never Seen So Far — One Unbroken 360° VR Flight Low Over the Vistula at Dusk, Poland
description:
This is not a tour. Nothing is pointed out to you.

One shot, no cuts. First so low that the water fills everything, then up over the willows until the whole valley is there at once.

"Down here the river will not hold still,
it argues with the light and breaks it small.
I took that for an answer once —
this close, you cannot read a thing at all.

I climbed above the willows and the wire,
and everything I dreaded came to rest:
the water was one road the whole time,
lying flat and patient toward the west."

The sun went down an hour before this was filmed. Look how much further you can see now.
